newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PBL up on pay TV rationalisation plan.
newsitem.headline: PBL up on pay TV rationalisation plan.

text.p: Shares in Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) rose over two percent in early trade on Monday following plans by key players in Australia's loss-making pay television industry to rationalise the sector.
At 11.40 a.m. (0145 GMT), PBL shares were 16 cents or 2.18 percent up at A$7.50, but just off its near 10 year high of A$7.60. Volume was light.

Late on Friday, PBL said it sold part of its interest in cash strapped satellite TV operator Australis Media Ltd to the owners of pay TV network Foxtel, News Corp Ltd and Telstra Corp Ltd as part of an industry shake-up.

Shares in Australis were also active, topping the share turnover lists with 9.67 million Australis shares traded, with the shares rising two cents to 14.5 cents by 11.50 p.m. (0150 GMT). News Corp shares were up 12 cents at A$6.40.
"There has been a flow of good news helping the stock and this is one of them," said one Sydney-based broker. He said PBL was not making any money from its Australis stake.
PBL has been touted as a bidder for newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd as part of the government's plans change Australia's media ownership laws.

"Some of the fears over Fairfax seems to be receding, as there is more and more talk that this thing (media ownership) was going to be pushed into some backroom (government) commitee," the broker said. Many investors had tipped PBL to make a share scrip offer for Fairfax.
Under the pay TV plan, News Corp said: "PBL will be given the opportunity to equalise its interests in pay tv with News interests." -- Kevin Morrison 61-2 9373-1813
